clue.text: Reporters curb drink and exercises

indicators.note: to curb is to hold in check, so the reporters' word closes round the drink's word

parts.note: the press is the collective term for reporters
to sup is to drink, sip

explanation.surface: Journalists are told to cut back their drinking and take some exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curb' reads as restraint of a habit, but it signals one word held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Push-ups lifting the body off the floor with the arms are a standard gym exercise.

clue.text: Violet's stabbing pain putting down flags

indicators.note: stabbing means the name for Violet pierces the word for a pain

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
Vi is a short form of the name Violet

explanation.surface: Violet is stabbed by pain while laying flagstones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' are flagstones, not banners; 'Violet's' means Violet is, doing the stabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying flagstones on a path is the work of covering it with slabs.

clue.text: Very probably see round Aussie now and then

indicators.note: round means the cathedral city's name goes round the letters picked

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a famous one in England

indicators.note: now and then means taking alternate letters of Aussie, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Very probably you will see an Australian round here from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a favourite crossword 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'it could easily rain', the word means very likely or quite possibly.

clue.text: Prime competition watched outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for watched sits round the word for competition

parts.note: seen means watched
an event is a sporting competition

explanation.surface: A main competition was watched from outside the venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like an adjective meaning chief, but it means a prime number.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime number has no divisors but itself and one; this is one such number.

clue.text: Where thirsty horse stops, luring in another one en route?

indicators.note: luring in means the place for horses draws another letter inside

parts.note: a horse on the road stops at a passing trough, a water trough by the roadside
another horse: H is slang for heroin, itself called horse

explanation.surface: A thirsty horse stops at a trough, perhaps tempting another one in along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'luring in' puts H inside TROUGH; 'horse' is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the way somewhere without stopping long is to be travelling en route.

clue.text: One gets Polish at Aldershot to step back

indicators.note: going back means the word for a step is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A soldier at the Aldershot garrison is told to buff his boots and step backwards on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldershot is a British Army garrison town, where boots are polished to a shine; the capital P of 'Polish' hides the plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The reinforced toe of a soldier's boot is the part buffed to a mirror shine on parade.

clue.text: Start off more promising element of basketwork

indicators.note: start off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: rosier means more promising, as in a rosier future

explanation.surface: Starting out on a more promising part of a basket-weaving project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' drops R from ROSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow whose pliant twigs are woven into baskets is a staple of the craft.

clue.text: Coach bearing fly trap

definitions.meaning: a coach is a horse-drawn vehicle
deportment, the way a person holds themselves
a fly is a light one-horse hackney vehicle
a trap is a light two-wheeled vehicle pulled by a pony

explanation.surface: A sports coach heading for a trap set for flies.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions: three horse-drawn vehicles plus a person's bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a horse-drawn vehicle and posture, the way a person holds themselves.

clue.text: Fool set up foil for one means of access

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sap is a fool
a foil is an example of a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A fool sets up a foil as one way of getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SAP into PAS; 'foil' is the fencing weapon, not a thwarting.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word typed at a login screen is what lets you get into an account.

clue.text: Exploit plot in gathering stock, improving plant conditions?

parts.note: a feat is an exploit, a bold deed

indicators.note: in means the plot word is placed inside the word for gathering livestock

parts.note: herding is gathering livestock together
a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A gardener's tip about exploiting a plot while gathering stock to improve growing conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' here is a factory: the term means overmanning and soft working practices, though 'plot' and 'stock' push a garden reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of keeping unnecessary jobs or easy rules makes a factory workforce comfortable.

clue.text: Having to deal with two foreign stamps? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite complete means the final letter of the doubled word is dropped
two means the stamp word appears twice in a row

parts.note: a visa is a stamp in a passport for entry to a foreign country

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders whether to deal with two foreign passport stamps, though not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' doubles VISA to VISAVISA and 'Not quite' drops the last A.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in English to mean regarding or in relation to something.

clue.text: European fighters ring about refugees

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the fighter planes surround the word for about

parts.note: MiGs are Russian fighter jets
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: European fighter jets circle above a group of refugees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is an encircling instruction; 'fighters' are aircraft, not soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have left their country, often for political reasons, are exiles who sought refuge abroad.

clue.text: Fabric label on bag briefly indicating transatlantic flight?

parts.note: a baggage tag shows airport codes; NY is short for New York
LON is short for London, so a tag reading NY-LON shows a flight across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: A luggage tag, in abbreviated form, shows a flight across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two short city names, New York and London, spell the material.
explanation.definitionFit: The synthetic material is a woven fabric used for stockings, bags and clothing.

clue.text: Grill Bury before contest with Wolves initially

parts.note: to inter is to bury
to vie is to compete, contest

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of Wolves is used

explanation.surface: Football talk: a grilling about Bury playing a match against Wolves.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury and Wolves (Wolverhampton Wanderers) are English football clubs, but here 'Bury' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to question them closely, as in a formal questioning session.

clue.text: Bugger Reg! I've cooked "healthy" food

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are rearranged, as in cooking the books

explanation.surface: An exasperated cook swears at Reg after making supposedly wholesome food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges BUGGER REG IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat-free patty in a bun is sold as wholesome fare, hence the ironic quotation marks.

clue.text: Nonstop ironing one might say put off Republican

indicators.note: put off means the letter for Republican is taken away

parts.note: ironing is taking the creases out, which one could call uncreasing

explanation.surface: Endless ironing, one might say, put off a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' removes R from UNCREASING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never ceases or stops is continuous, without a break.

clue.text: Leaving party or a job, say, after reorganisation

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: after reorganisation means the letters of say are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a political party, or a job, after a restructuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reorganisation' scrambles only the last word, 'say'; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Renouncing a religion or political allegiance is defection from one's faith or cause.

clue.text: Well-known solver in Paris breaking US laws

indicators.note: breaking means the French word splits the country's name

parts.note: the US is the United States, the States
the solver is you, addressed familiarly; the familiar French you is tu

explanation.surface: A famous Parisian puzzler breaks American laws.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver is 'you', addressed in the familiar form, as one well known to the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written rules passed by a legislature, acts of parliament.

clue.text: Praise and thank beat cop after refreshment

indicators.note: after refreshment means the words are made new, refreshed into a different order

explanation.surface: Praise and thanks go to a beat cop who has just had a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refreshment' looks like a cup of tea, but 'after refreshment' asks for a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means congratulating someone, like a literal gesture of approval between shoulders.

clue.text: Needlework's rubbish on top of this

parts.note: tat is rubbish, cheap tasteless goods
too means also, on top of this

explanation.surface: Someone's needlework is rubbish, and that comes on top of everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needlework' is skin art done with needles, not sewing; in a down clue 'on top of' looks positional.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink pricked into skin with needles is literally work done with a needle.

clue.text: Set erected around each cold stormy location?

indicators.note: around means the turned word goes round the letters for each and cold
erected means the word for set is raised up, read from bottom to top in this down clue

parts.note: to put is to set down
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A set is put up around each cold, stormy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns the word upward in this down clue; 'around' then wraps it about two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a storm in a teacup' names this as the setting for a fuss over nothing.

clue.text: What arboreal picnickers did that's useful to joiner?

definitions.text: What arboreal picnickers did that's useful to joiner?

parts.words: What arboreal picnickers did that's useful to joiner?
parts.note: picnickers among trees sat in a wood; split differently the phrase is a timber prized by cabinetmakers

explanation.surface: A riddle about picnickers among the trees and what a carpenter would want.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard, glossy yellowish timber is used by cabinetmakers and joiners for fine furniture.

clue.text: Green unit fills part of church

indicators.note: fills means the unit letter goes inside the church word

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I, the numeral one, is a unit

explanation.surface: An environmental group fills part of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fills' puts I inside NAVE; 'Green' is inexperienced, not ecological.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or gullible, lacking worldly wisdom.

clue.text: A feature of Hampton Court floor

parts.note: Hampton Court Palace near London has a famous hedge maze

explanation.surface: Describing a floor that is a feature of Hampton Court palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is the verb, to stun; Hampton Court is a royal palace by the Thames with a famous hedge maze.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to astonish or dumbfound them.

clue.text: A large item making up Reykjavik diet

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
an item is a thing

explanation.surface: A big item makes up the diet of someone in Reykjavik.
explanation.walkthrough: A diet is also a legislative assembly; this is Iceland's parliament, which sits in Reykjavik.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland's national parliament is the assembly that governs from the capital, Reykjavik.

clue.text: Absurd papers to do with hearing absorb one

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so the two words close round the numeral one

parts.note: ID means identity papers
otic means relating to the ear
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Papers about a hearing take in one person, absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court hearing; 'absorb' puts the numeral between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foolish or ridiculous is absurd, the kind of thing a fool would do.

clue.text: Poodles long to grab odd bits of jetsam

indicators.note: to grab means the word for long takes hold of the letters in its middle

parts.note: to yen is to long for

indicators.note: odd bits means alternate letters of jetsam are taken, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Poodles longing to snatch scraps of flotsam and jetsam on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' here takes the even-placed letters; 'to grab' then wraps the word for long round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle, figuratively, is a servile follower who always agrees with a superior.

clue.text: Cohort mature twice, shedding weight

parts.note: to age is to mature

indicators.note: shedding means a letter is dropped from the second phrase for mature

parts.note: twice means a second word for mature is needed: grow up

explanation.surface: Someone matures twice over while losing weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' asks for two synonyms of mature: AGE and GROW UP; 'shedding' removes W from GROWUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a set of people of similar age, studied as one band.
